theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Energy (+1.25%) and Consumer Staples (+1.17%) led the market today, while Technology (-1.23%) and Consumer Discretionary (-0.51%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.26% versus +0.82% for defensives and +0.50% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.06%, Dow +0.38%, Nasdaq -0.44% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -0.45%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 2.49% to 15.21, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.84% to $4,191.80, crude oil was little changed at $92.60, and bitcoin gained 1.12% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
